Garlic bits still lodge in the hinge and holes eventually, so 'one-wipe' is the easy days, not every day

Beveled holes push out a fine, even mince rather than crushed chunks
Solid stainless steel body with a long ergonomic lever that lowers the squeeze effort

name: Stagg EKG Electric Gooseneck Kettle (0.9L)

name: BenQ ScreenBar Monitor Light Bar
keySpec: Clips over any monitor (no desk footprint), asymmetric optics throw light on the desk not the screen (zero glare), auto-dimming ambient sensor, adjustable brightness.
blurb: Clips onto your monitor to light your desk without throwing any glare on the screen, and takes up zero desk space. It auto-dims to match the room.
verdict: A monitor-mounted light bar that lights your desk and papers without bouncing glare back at the screen, and reclaims the space a desk lamp would eat. The price is high for a light, but it solves the glare-and-clutter problem cleanly for a monitor setup.
bestFor: The desk worker in a dim room whose monitor picks up glare from every lamp they have tried
cons: At $99-109 it is expensive next to a basic desk lamp that also produces light
The clip is designed for flat-backed monitors, so very thick, very thin, curved, or all-in-one screens like an iMac can fit poorly or not at all
It draws power over USB, so it occupies a port and needs one within reach
keyFeatures: Clips over the top of the monitor, adding light with zero desk footprint
Asymmetric optics throw light down onto the desk instead of onto the screen, avoiding glare
Ambient light sensor auto-dims the bar to match the room
Adjustable brightness for reading, notes, or evening work
whyItMatters: A normal desk lamp near a monitor either wastes space or reflects glare onto the screen, and this fixes both by lighting only what is below the display.
buyingNotes: Before buying, check your monitor's top edge: the weighted clip is engineered for flat-backed panels and perches poorly on very thin, curved, or all-in-one screens like an iMac. It powers over USB, so you need a free USB-A port on the monitor, laptop, or dock, or a USB wall adapter within cable reach. This base ScreenBar controls brightness and color temperature with touch buttons on the bar itself; the wireless remote and back-glow belong to the pricier ScreenBar Halo.

faq.q: Will it fit a curved or ultrawide monitor?
faq.a: The clip is designed for flat-backed monitors and seats securely on those. On a curved or ultrawide panel it can balance on the flattest part of the top edge, but the fit is less stable, and a very thin or all-in-one screen like an iMac is a poor match.

faq.q: Does it reflect glare onto the screen?
faq.a: No, and that is its main design point. The asymmetric optics throw light down onto the desk and keyboard rather than back at the display, which is why it suits people who get glare from a normal desk lamp.

faq.q: How is it powered?
faq.a: Over USB. It draws from a USB-A port on your monitor, laptop, dock, or a USB wall adapter, so there is no separate power brick, but it does occupy a USB port within cable reach.

whoShouldAvoid: Skip it if you have a curved, ultra-thin, or all-in-one screen like an iMac. The clip is engineered for flat-backed monitors and won't seat securely on those shapes.
mainTradeoff: You pay roughly triple the cost of a basic desk lamp for the zero-glare, zero-footprint trick of lighting the desk without hitting the screen.
whatCouldChange: Cheaper clip-on bars (including no-name copies) do the same asymmetric-light trick; if you can live without the auto-dimming ambient sensor a ~$30 version may be enough, so first confirm your monitor's top edge is flat.

name: Rain Design mStand Aluminum Laptop Stand (Silver, 10032)
keySpec: Single-piece anodized aluminum, raises screen 5.9 in to eye level, doubles as a heat sink, rear cable routing hole, sturdy MacBook-matching finish.
blurb: Raises your laptop screen almost 6 inches to eye level so you stop hunching, and the solid aluminum body doubles as a heat sink to keep it cool.
verdict: A solid, single-piece aluminum stand that lifts your laptop to eye level and doubles as a heat sink, with a look that matches a MacBook. Great as a permanent home-desk fixture; the fixed height and heft make it wrong for anyone who wants adjustability or portability.
bestFor: The person working from a fixed home desk who hunches over a laptop all day and already has an external keyboard and mouse
cons: The height is fixed at 5.9 inches, so it only lands at eye level if that rise happens to match your chair and desk
Raising the screen puts the laptop keyboard out of comfortable reach, so you effectively must add an external keyboard and mouse
It is a heavy, solid piece meant to stay put, not a foldable travel stand
keyFeatures: Machined from a single piece of anodized aluminum for a sturdy, no-wobble base
Raises the screen about 5.9 inches toward eye level to reduce neck hunching
Aluminum body doubles as a heat sink to help the laptop run cooler
Rear cable-routing hole keeps charger and accessory cords tidy
whyItMatters: Typing on a laptop pulls the screen down and your neck with it, and lifting the display to eye height is the core fix for that daily strain.
buyingNotes: This is a fixed-height fixture, so it only lands your screen at eye level if a 5.9-inch rise happens to suit your chair-and-desk height; measure before you commit. Raising the screen puts the laptop's own keyboard out of comfortable reach, so budget for an external keyboard and mouse too. It is a heavy single-piece stand meant to live on one desk, not fold into a bag, so if you move around look at a foldable travel stand instead.

faq.q: Does it fit any laptop or just MacBooks?
faq.a: The aluminum finish is styled to match a MacBook, but the open cradle holds most 13-to-16-inch laptops. The fit is universal; only the look is Mac-flavored.

faq.q: Can I keep typing on the laptop after raising it?
faq.a: Not comfortably. Lifting the screen about six inches pushes the built-in keyboard up and away, so the stand assumes you will pair it with a separate keyboard and mouse.

faq.q: Does it actually help cooling?
faq.a: The solid aluminum body draws heat away and the open design lets air move under the laptop, so it runs a little cooler than sitting flat on a desk. It is a passive heat sink, not active cooling.

whoShouldAvoid: Skip it if you move between spots or want to keep typing on the laptop's own keyboard. It's a heavy, fixed-height fixture that pushes the built-in keyboard out of reach and forces an external keyboard and mouse.
mainTradeoff: You give up all adjustability and portability in exchange for a rock-solid, single-piece aluminum base that also acts as a heat sink.
whatCouldChange: The 5.9-inch rise only lands at eye level if it happens to match your chair and desk; if it doesn't, an adjustable or foldable stand fits your body better, so verify the height works for you before buying.

name: Stand Up Desk Store Under-Desk Cable Management Tray (Black, 51 in)

faq.a: Yes. It attaches with screws into the desk underside, and that is what keeps it rigid under the weight of a power strip and adapters. If you cannot drill, a no-install cable box or adhesive raceway is the renter-friendly alternative.

faq.a: It is 51 inches long, built for a full-width standing desk. On a narrower desk it will overhang the ends, so measure before buying.

faq.q: What does it actually hold?
faq.a: A power strip plus the slack cord and adapters, lifted off the floor. It also doubles as a modesty panel that hides the cable tangle from anyone standing behind the desk.

mainTradeoff: You accept a permanent drill-in install (done awkwardly overhead) to get the power strip and cords fully off the floor and hidden behind the desk.
whatCouldChange: If you can't or won't drill, a no-install cable box or adhesive raceway is the renter-friendly alternative; also confirm your desk is wide enough for the 51-inch tray.

keyFeatures: Encloses a power strip and its excess cord so a desk or console looks finished
Dedicated cord outlets let cables exit cleanly on each side

Neutral finish blends into most desk and living-room decor
whyItMatters: A power strip and its coil of slack cord is often the one thing that makes an otherwise tidy surface look messy, and this simply puts a lid on it.
buyingNotes: Measure your power strip against the roughly 12 x 5 x 4.5-inch interior before buying, since a bulky surge protector or several large GaN bricks may not fit. Because it is a closed box it traps heat, so keep hard-working, high-draw adapters out of it and use it for low-draw phone and device chargers. It hides one visible spot rather than routing cables across a whole desk, so treat it as a cover-up, not a full cable-management system.

faq.q: Is it safe to put a power strip inside a closed box?
faq.a: It is designed for exactly that with low-draw chargers, but any enclosed box traps heat. Keep high-wattage, hard-working adapters out of it and do not overfill it; for light phone and device charging it is fine.

faq.q: Will my power strip fit?
faq.a: The interior is about 12 x 5 x 4.5 inches. A standard slim strip fits; a large surge protector or a strip loaded with big bricks may not, so measure first.

faq.q: Is the lid real wood?
faq.a: No, it is a wood-look plastic finish. It blends into desk or living-room decor from a normal viewing distance but is not genuine wood up close.

whoShouldAvoid: Skip it if you're stuffing a bulky surge protector or hard-working GaN charging bricks inside. The 12 x 5 x 4.5-inch interior runs tight and the closed box traps heat around high-draw adapters.
mainTradeoff: It hides the clutter of one visible spot rather than actually routing cables across a whole setup.
whatCouldChange: If you need to manage cables across an entire desk, a mounted raceway or tray does more; measure your power strip against the 12-inch interior first, since large bricks may not fit.

name: Anker Prime 6-in-1 Charging Station (140W)
keySpec: 2 AC outlets + 2 USB-C + 2 USB-A, 140W max, slim 0.7 in profile, real-time smart power display, 5 ft detachable extension cord.
blurb: One slim hub with 2 outlets and 4 USB ports delivers up to 140W, enough to fast-charge a laptop and phone at once and clear away a tangle of wall plugs.
verdict: A slim desktop hub that combines two AC outlets and four USB ports with up to 140W and a live power readout, replacing a wad of wall plugs. Strong for a laptop-and-phone desk; just know the 140W is shared across everything, not delivered to each port at once.
bestFor: The desk worker who wants to fast-charge a USB-C laptop and phone plus power a couple of accessories from one tidy hub
cons: The 140W is a shared total, so loading up all the ports splits the power rather than giving each device its own max
At $90-110 it costs far more than a plain power strip with USB ports
It is a tethered desktop unit on a 5 ft cord, built to sit on a desk rather than travel
keyFeatures: 2 AC outlets plus 2 USB-C and 2 USB-A ports in one unit
Up to 140W total, enough to fast-charge a USB-C laptop and a phone together
Slim 0.7 in profile with a 5 ft detachable extension cord to reach the wall
Real-time smart power display shows how much each side is drawing
whyItMatters: A modern desk collects a laptop brick, a phone charger, and a pile of wall plugs, and this folds them into one slim hub with a single cord to the wall.
buyingNotes: The 140W is a shared total across all ports, not per-port, so if you plan to fast-charge a laptop and phone at once, check that their combined peak draw fits under 140W; loading all six ports splits the power. faq.q: Is the 140W available on every port at once?
faq.a: No. 140W is the combined budget shared across all six ports. One USB-C port can pull most of it for a laptop, but plugging in more devices divides the total rather than giving each its full max.

faq.q: Can it fast-charge a USB-C laptop?
faq.a: Yes, a single USB-C port can deliver enough to fast-charge most USB-C laptops, and you can still run a phone and a couple of accessories alongside as long as you stay under the 140W total.

faq.q: What does the display show?
faq.a: A real-time readout of how much power the unit is delivering, so you can see the draw of what is plugged in. It is a monitoring convenience, not a separate meter for every port.

whoShouldAvoid: Skip it if you just need to power a few low-draw devices. A plain power strip with USB ports costs a fraction of the $90-110 price and does that job fine.
mainTradeoff: The 140W is a shared total, so loading up all six ports splits the power rather than giving each device its own max.
whatCouldChange: If you don't fast-charge a USB-C laptop, a cheaper USB power strip covers you; check that the 140W shared total actually meets your laptop-plus-phone peak draw before relying on it.

verdict: A rechargeable Bluetooth tracker that works with either Apple Find My or Google Find Hub and tops up over USB-C instead of eating coin cells. Best for Android users or anyone who wants a rechargeable AirTag alternative, though it lacks the ultra-wideband pinpoint finding an AirTag has on iPhone.
bestFor: Android users who want an AirTag-style tracker that works on the Google Find Hub network
cons: It pairs with one network at a time, so you choose either Apple or Google, not both at once
Without ultra-wideband it can't pinpoint the last few feet the way an AirTag's Precision Finding does on iPhone

keyFeatures: Compatibility with both Apple Find My and Google Find Hub networks (pick one at setup)
USB-C recharging that skips replaceable coin cells
A loud 130dB siren and bright LED strobe to home in on it up close
An IP66 water-resistant clip body that attaches to keys or a bag
whyItMatters: It finds misplaced keys, bags, or a remote, and it's one of the few trackers that serves Android's Find Hub network as well as Apple's.
buyingNotes: Unlike an AirTag, the Clip 5 works with both Apple Find My and Google Find Hub, but you pick one network at setup; it cannot run on both at once, so decide which you need. It has no ultra-wideband chip, so it cannot pinpoint the last few feet the way an AirTag's Precision Finding does on an iPhone. For an all-Apple household a 4-pack of AirTags is often cheaper per tag, so this really wins for Android users or anyone who specifically wants USB-C recharging over replaceable coin cells.

faq.q: Does it work with Android?
faq.a: Yes. It is one of the few trackers that supports Google's Find Hub network as well as Apple Find My. You choose one network when you set it up.

faq.q: Do I have to replace batteries?
faq.a: No. It recharges over USB-C, with a charge lasting roughly a year, so there are no coin cells to buy and swap like on an AirTag.

faq.q: Can it pinpoint items as precisely as an AirTag?
faq.a: Not the final few feet, since it lacks the ultra-wideband chip AirTags use for Precision Finding on iPhone. It does have a loud 130dB siren and LED strobe to help you home in by sound and sight.

whoShouldAvoid: Skip it if you live entirely in Apple's world and want the tightest last-few-feet pinpoint: it has no ultra-wideband chip, so a plain AirTag's Precision Finding will home in more precisely on an iPhone.
mainTradeoff: You give up an AirTag's ultra-wideband pinpoint homing in exchange for cross-platform flexibility (Apple Find My or Google Find Hub) and a USB-C rechargeable battery instead of replaceable coin cells.
whatCouldChange: For an all-Apple household a 4-pack of AirTags is usually cheaper per tag and adds Precision Finding, so this really wins for Android users or anyone who specifically wants USB-C recharging over coin cells; note it pairs to only one network at a time, so confirm which you need before buying.

name: HyperChiller HC2 Rapid Iced Coffee / Beverage Cooler
keySpec: Cools hot coffee up to 130°F in about 60 seconds with NO dilution; freeze the inner chamber, pour hot in, pour cold out; also chills wine/liquor/tea; dishwasher-safe.
blurb: Chills hot coffee to iced in about a minute without watering it down: freeze the inner chamber, pour hot in, and pour cold out. It also cools wine, liquor, or tea, and is dishwasher-safe.
verdict: A single-serve gadget that chills hot coffee to iced in about a minute without watering it down, so you skip the freezer-ice dilution and the overnight cold-brew wait. Worth it if iced coffee is a daily ritual and you hate a diluted cup.
bestFor: the daily hot-brew drinker who wants iced coffee immediately without melting ice diluting the flavor
cons: The inner chamber has to be pre-frozen, so it needs permanent freezer space and a little planning before your first cup of the day

Multiple stacking parts mean it must be dried fully between uses or frost builds up, and assembly matters or it can leak
keyFeatures: Cools coffee up to 130 F to iced in about 60 seconds by pouring hot in and cold out
Chills without adding ice, so the coffee's strength and flavor stay intact
Doubles as a fast chiller for wine, liquor, and tea, not just coffee
Dishwasher-safe parts for cleanup
whyItMatters: It solves the everyday annoyance of iced coffee that's either watery from melting ice or hours away via cold brew.

name: Dreamfarm Scizza Non-Stick Pizza Scissors
keySpec: Pizza scissors with a built-in non-stick server 'spatula' base that slides under the crust; cuts without dragging toppings; won't scratch pans or trays; dishwasher-safe.
blurb: Scissors that cut pizza cleanly without dragging cheese and toppings out of place, with a non-stick server base that slides under each slice to lift it out. It won't scratch pans or trays.
verdict: Kitchen scissors with a built-in non-stick base plate that slides under the crust as you cut, so slices come out clean instead of shredded with toppings dragged everywhere. A niche tool, but if you make or order pizza often it earns its spot.
bestFor: the frequent home-pizza or frozen-pizza eater who's tired of a wheel cutter dragging cheese off the slice
cons: It's priced like a good pair of shears for a single job, so occasional pizza nights won't justify it
The flat server base makes it bulkier and more awkward to store than a compact pizza wheel
Very thick deep-dish or a rock-hard crispy crust can tax the scissor action more than a rolling cutter would
keyFeatures: Scissor cut slices through cheese and toppings without dragging them out of place
Non-stick server base slides under the crust to lift each slice straight out
Base plate protects pans, trays, and stones from scratches
Dishwasher-safe for cleanup
whyItMatters: It fixes the way a pizza wheel drags toppings off the slice and scratches your pan on the way through.

name: Besmon Electric Automatic Jar Opener (Hands-Free)
keySpec: One-touch automatic jar opener; grips the lid and unscrews hands-free after a 3-second press; fits a wide range of screw-cap jar sizes; battery-powered.
blurb: Sits on top of a stuck jar, grips the lid, and twists it off hands-free after a single press, sparing weak or aching wrists. It fits a wide range of screw-cap sizes and runs on batteries.
verdict: A battery-powered gadget that grips a stuck lid and unscrews it hands-free after one press, aimed squarely at weak, arthritic, or aching wrists. Genuinely useful as an accessibility aid, less compelling if you just want to open the occasional pickle jar.
bestFor: someone with arthritis or limited hand strength who struggles to open jars unaided
cons: It runs on batteries, so there's ongoing replacement and it won't work if they die mid-jar
The motorized unit is bulky and takes real drawer or counter space compared with a manual grip pad
It only handles screw-cap jars, not pry-off, cork, or push-and-turn childproof lids
keyFeatures: One 3-second press and it grips and unscrews the lid fully hands-free
Auto-adjusts to fit a wide range of screw-cap jar diameters
Battery-powered, so it works anywhere without a plug
Sits on top of the jar and does the twisting, requiring almost no grip strength
whyItMatters: It restores the everyday independence of opening a jar for people whose hands or wrists can't manage the force.

name: MX Master 3S Wireless Performance Mouse (Graphite)
keySpec: 8,000 DPI Darkfield sensor (tracks on glass), MagSpeed electromagnetic scroll wheel (1,000 lines/sec), near-silent Quiet Clicks, USB-C fast charge (~70 days per charge).
blurb: A precise, near-silent mouse whose fast MagSpeed wheel flies through long documents, and it flows across several computers on a charge that lasts weeks.
verdict: Logitech's flagship productivity mouse, built around a fast electromagnetic scroll wheel, near-silent clicks, and multi-computer flow, making it a strong pick for anyone who works in long documents and spreadsheets all day. Overkill and the wrong shape for gaming or small hands.
bestFor: the desk worker who scrolls through long docs, code, or spreadsheets and juggles more than one computer
cons: The large, sculpted right-hand shape excludes lefties and doesn't suit small hands or a fingertip grip
It's priced well above a basic wireless mouse
Getting the most from the buttons and gestures means installing Logi Options+ software, which some find heavy
keyFeatures: MagSpeed wheel free-spins through long pages and ratchets for precise line-by-line control
Quiet Clicks cut the noise of every press without losing the tactile feel
Darkfield 8,000 DPI sensor tracks on nearly any surface, including glass
USB-C fast charging with battery life measured in weeks, plus flow across multiple computers
whyItMatters: It solves the wrist fatigue and slow navigation of scrolling through long documents on a basic mouse.
buyingNotes: This is a large, right-hand-sculpted mouse, so it is wrong for left-handers, small hands, or a fingertip grip; check the shape suits your hand before buying. It is priced well above a basic wireless mouse, and getting the most from the extra buttons and gestures means installing Logitech's Options+ software. If you game, choose a low-latency gaming mouse instead, since this is built for productivity, not fast play.

faq.q: Is there a left-handed version?
faq.a: No. The MX Master 3S is sculpted for the right hand only. Left-handers should look at an ambidextrous mouse like Logitech's MX Anywhere or a symmetrical model.

faq.q: Is it good for gaming?
faq.a: No. It is a productivity mouse tuned for scrolling and precision work, not the low-latency response gaming needs. A dedicated gaming mouse is the better pick there.

faq.q: Do I need the software?
faq.a: The mouse works out of the box, but the customizable buttons, gestures, and app-specific scrolling need Logitech Options+ installed to configure. Without it you get standard mouse functions only.

whoShouldAvoid: Skip it if you're left-handed, have small hands or use a fingertip grip, or game. It's a large right-hand-sculpted productivity mouse, wrong for all of those.
mainTradeoff: You pay well above a basic wireless mouse for the fast MagSpeed scroll wheel, near-silent Quiet Clicks, and multi-computer flow.
whatCouldChange: If you want the ergonomics without the flagship price, Logitech's cheaper models share the Options+ software and gestures; gamers should choose a low-latency gaming mouse instead, so check the right-hand shape fits your grip.

name: TS4 18-Port Thunderbolt 4 Dock (Space Gray)

verdict: CalDigit's top-tier Thunderbolt 4 dock turns a laptop into a full desktop over one cable, with more ports than almost anything else and 98W charging. It's the reference-grade choice, but the price and the Thunderbolt requirement make it overkill for a simple two-accessory setup.
bestFor: the laptop-as-desktop professional running dual monitors, wired networking, and storage from one connection

Base-model Apple Silicon Macs still drive only one external display no matter how capable the dock is

Drives a single 8K display or dual 6K monitors at 60Hz
whyItMatters: It replaces a tangle of separate adapters and chargers with one cable that connects everything at once.
buyingNotes: To unlock the full display bandwidth you need a Thunderbolt 4 or USB4 host; on a slower USB-C laptop it still works but you lose the top display and speed potential. Note that base-model Apple Silicon Macs (the standard M-series MacBook Air and Pro) still drive only one external display no matter how capable the dock is, so verify your Mac supports dual monitors before buying for that. At $370-400 it is reference-grade, so a simple two-accessory setup will never use all 18 ports, and a cheaper USB-C hub covers that.

faq.q: Can I run two external monitors?
faq.a: The dock can drive dual 6K displays, but your computer has to support that. A base-model Apple Silicon Mac only outputs to one external display regardless of the dock, so check your machine's multi-monitor limit first.

faq.q: Do I need a Thunderbolt laptop?
faq.a: For full performance, yes. A Thunderbolt 4 or USB4 host unlocks the 40Gb/s bandwidth and top display support. It will still function on a plain USB-C port, but you will not get the full capability you are paying for.

faq.q: Does it charge my laptop?
faq.a: Yes, it delivers up to 98W of charging over the single host cable, enough to power most laptops while it also connects all your peripherals.

whoShouldAvoid: Skip it if you only plug in a couple of accessories, or if you run a base-model Apple Silicon Mac. That Mac still drives just one external display no matter how capable the dock is.
mainTradeoff: You pay $370-400 reference-grade dock money for far more ports and bandwidth than a simple two-accessory setup will ever use.
whatCouldChange: Without a Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 host you can't unlock its full display and bandwidth, and a cheaper USB-C hub covers a light setup; verify your laptop's host port and multi-display support first.

name: LX Single Monitor Arm, Desk Mount (Matte Black)

bestFor: someone reclaiming desk space and dialing in ergonomic height for a monitor up to 34 inches
cons: It costs noticeably more than budget gas-spring arms that look similar on paper

It needs either a desk edge to clamp to or a grommet hole, and heavier ultrawides sit best near the low end of its range
keyFeatures: Patented Constant Force spring holds the screen at any height without slow sag

Clears the desktop underneath for a cleaner, more usable workspace

It costs noticeably more than look-alike gas-spring arms, and you are paying for the constant-force spring and metal build that will not slowly sag over time.

faq.q: Will it hold my monitor at any height?
faq.a: Yes, that is the point of the constant-force spring. It holds the screen wherever you set it without the slow downward drift cheaper gas-spring arms develop, as long as your monitor is within the 7-25 lb range.

faq.q: How does it attach to the desk?
faq.a: It clamps to a desk edge or mounts through a grommet hole, both included. You need one of those; it cannot attach to a desk with no accessible edge or hole.

faq.q: What monitor sizes and weights does it fit?
faq.a: Flat, curved, and ultrawide monitors up to 34 inches and between 7 and 25 pounds. Heavier ultrawides sit best toward the lower end of its extension range.

whoShouldAvoid: Skip it if your monitor is very light (under about 7 lb). Below the arm's minimum weight the constant-force spring can float the screen up instead of holding it where you set it.
mainTradeoff: You pay noticeably more than look-alike budget gas-spring arms for the constant-force spring and metal build that won't slowly sag.
whatCouldChange: If your monitor is light or your budget is tight, a cheaper gas-spring arm may do; confirm your monitor lands in the 7-25 lb range and that you have a desk edge to clamp to or a grommet hole to mount through.

name: Q1 Pro QMK/VIA Wireless Custom Mechanical Keyboard (75%)

name: Breville Barista Express Espresso Machine (BES870XL)

name: Vitamix 5200 Professional-Grade Blender (64 oz)

name: Peak Design Everyday Backpack 20L (V2)

faq.a: The 420HC stainless is tough and easy to resharpen, which suits a hard-working multitool, but it will not hold an edge as long as a dedicated premium knife. The wire cutters are replaceable, which extends the tool's usable life.

whoShouldAvoid: Someone who wants a light, truly pocketable everyday carry should skip it: the Wave+ is heavy and thick enough that most owners end up belt-carrying it in a sheath. If you only need scissors and a driver on your keys, the Micra is the lighter pick.

whatCouldChange: No pocket clip or sheath comes in the box, so budget for one to carry it comfortably. And if edge retention matters more than versatility, the 420HC steel won't hold an edge as long as a dedicated premium knife.

bestFor: the traveler who wants one charger for a laptop, phone, and earbuds instead of a bag full of bricks

keyFeatures: 100W total GaN output that pushes a single USB-C port up to 100W, enough to fast-charge a MacBook Pro

PPS support for fast, efficient charging on compatible phones like recent Samsung Galaxy models
Foldable prongs and a body around 35% smaller than a stock laptop brick for easy packing

No charging cable is included, so factor in a USB-C cable you supply yourself. If you only ever charge one device, a smaller single-port GaN charger is lighter and cheaper for the same job.

whoShouldAvoid: Someone who only ever charges one device should skip it: you would be paying for three ports and shared 100W you won't use, when a single-port GaN charger is smaller and cheaper for the same laptop-charging job.
mainTradeoff: You collapse a laptop, phone, and earbuds brick into one packable GaN unit, but the 100W is a shared budget, so plugging in a second device drops the top USB-C port well below its full 100W.
whatCouldChange: No USB-C cable is included, so factor that added cost in. And if you need full-speed simultaneous laptop-plus-phone charging rather than split power, look at a higher-wattage 140W unit instead.
